title: Unitary Foundation Launches Its 2026 Quantum Open Source Software Survey - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The Unitary Foundation launched its annual 2026 Quantum Open Source Software (QOSS) survey to map the quantum open-source community's demographics, research, tools and platforms. The article states a close date of October 29, 2025, apparently a typo for 2026, given the October 2026 publication date.

insights.claim: The Unitary Foundation has launched its 2026 Quantum Open Source Software (QOSS) survey, covering demographics, research, tools and platforms of the quantum open-source community.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: The results will be a public data source on which quantum software tools and platforms the developer community uses.

insights.claim: The Unitary Foundation has run the QOSS survey yearly since 2022, giving a multi-year series for tracking how the quantum open-source community evolves.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Year-over-year results can show shifts in tool and platform adoption among quantum developers.
insights.quote: This is a yearly survey that the Unitary Foundation has been doing since 2022.

insights.claim: Anonymized QOSS results will be analyzed and shared publicly by the Unitary Foundation as a resource on the field's tools, research and resources.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Watch the published results for adoption signals across quantum SDKs and platforms.

insights.claim: The survey is positioned to help stakeholders improve their quantum products, services and events to better accommodate users, so it works as a demand-side signal for vendors.
insights.speaker: Doug Finke
insights.so_what: Quantum software vendors can use the results to prioritize developer-facing features.
